problem.text: LinearFP16.forward zero-filled an output buffer immediately before matrix multiplication wrote its result into it.

reasoning.text: Replacing zeros with empty removes initialization work. The existing Torch branch supplies out=y; the native branch uses alpha=1 and beta=0, requesting a product without accumulating the previous output.

impact.text: Output dimensions, device, bias addition and final reshaping remain unchanged. Any latency improvement is unmeasured.

source_notes.text: The root quantized-inference entry establishes the dense backend’s original role; the later dtype-dispatch entry explains the existing Torch/native split and native half-input restriction. Both entries were read.
Issue #39, “Gemma 3 architecture not in list?”, concerns architecture availability and subsequent frontend discussion, not evidence validating this output-allocation change.

limitations: No GPU execution, numerical comparison or benchmark was performed. A scalar arithmetic model would not validate Torch/cuBLAS output-buffer behavior or allocation performance.

Successful output production still depends on the selected multiplication backend. Native hgemm checks half inputs and compatible rank-two shapes, but does not inspect cuBLAS return statuses; backend failure behavior with an uninitialized output was not tested.

chapters.title: Allocate dense linear output without zero filling

claims.text: The buffer remains a flattened-row-count × out_features tensor. Matching input/output dtypes select torch.matmul; differing dtypes select ext.hgemm. Both precede the optional in-place bias addition, so successful multiplication supplies the initialization that bias addition needs.

The accompanying dtype edit replaces first_not_none with an or chain: call override, instance default, then torch.half. The old helper explicitly skipped only None; the new expression skips false-valued objects. The declared interface remains torch.dtype or None, and the now-unused helper import remains.
The optimization trades a guaranteed zeroed allocation for reliance on the already-present overwrite operation; it does not introduce buffer reuse or fuse bias into multiplication.

annotation.summary: LinearFP16 uses an uninitialized output buffer instead of zero filling it and simplifies dtype fallback. Existing multiplication supplies the output values; performance remains unmeasured.
